items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: Mr. LaRocca has told me that you have made wrongful claims regarding the part that you have played in the world of jazz music... and in some instances, I have been advised that you have made absolutely false and unfounded statements regarding your relationship with the original Dixieland jazz band

ctx.x: Yeah, I'll read Brown's letter now. His answer to Mr. Clinton.

Tom, this is letter headed. Tom Brown's Music Shop, Musical Instruments and Supplies. It was at 3027 Magazine Street. He has that marked out. His new address is 1228th Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. October 21st, 1957. Herman and Herman, 107 Cam Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. Dear Sir, semicolon dash. I received a letter dated October 14th, address, comma, address to me, comma, and the enclosure written to Harry Sushant of the New Orleans Jazz Club. I opened the letter because my name was on the envelope,…

to do, comma, according to the letter, comma, but I would rather hear from you to write, comma, that's capital B-U-T, new paragraph, it sounds like another jazz stunt to me, comma, new paragraph, this matter has been lingering for a good many years, and if they do not know who is the right introducer of jazz is by now, comma, they will never know, comma, hoping to receive an early reply from you, that's a new paragraph, hoping to receive an early reply from you, yours truly, comma, Tom Brown, it's Tom Brown,…
